hints: The XOR of two bit strings has ones exactly where they differ.
Count those one bits with a population-count operation.
Compare every pair, using a machine word because k is at most 30.
analogy: XOR marks the disagreements between two answer sheets.
example: The strings 1010 and 1110 differ only in their second bit, so their Hamming distance is 1.
algorithm: Convert each binary string to an integer. For each unordered pair, compute XOR and count its set bits; keep the minimum. A zero result is optimal and allows an immediate stop.
correctness: Each XOR bit is one exactly when the corresponding input bits differ, so its population count is the Hamming distance. Inspecting all pairs finds the minimum.
complexity: For n strings of k bits fitting one machine word, O(n^2+nk) time with constant-time population count and O(n) space.
